# Thanksgiving Hymns Column 27 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 1QHa (Cave 1), Col. 27 | **Condition:** very fragmentary

---

**1** [...] all [...] You have created for Your glory, and [...] according to [...]

**2** [...] the host of Your works, and You have assigned [...] in the service of [...]

**3** [...] Your truth. And You have established the generations of [...] for all [...]

**4** [...] the appointed times of eternity, and the seasons of [...] You determined [...]

**5** [...] to walk before You in the land of the living, and You have opened [...]

**6** [...] the springs of [...] for Your servant, and the wellspring of [...] truth [...]

**7** [...] for the sake of Your glory. And You created the breath [...]

**8** [...] of every living creature, and the ordering of all their works You determined [...]

**9** [...] and the mighty ones who carry out Your will, and [...] for Your glory [...]

**10** [...] You have created [...] for Your honor and for the sake of Your name [...]

**11** [...] and the spirits [...] their appointed tasks You have allotted to them [...]

**12** [...] among the holy ones, and [...] the host of the angels [...]

**13** [...] You have assigned their service before Your glory [...]

**14** [...] and the princes of [...] in their dominions [...]

**15** [...] the luminaries according to their mysteries, and the stars [...]

**16** [...] the winds according to their appointed laws, and all their works [...]

**17** [...] according to their generations, and the storehouses [...]

**18** [...] lightning and snow and [...] ice [...]

**19** [...] in their appointed seasons for [...] Your purpose [...]

**20** [...] for You have established all of them for Your glory [...]

---

*LOGOS notes: Column 27 is very fragmentary, situated near the end of the scroll. The preserved text is a cosmic hymn assigning both angelic beings and natural phenomena to their divinely appointed roles. The refrain "for Your glory" structures the column's theology. "Host of the angels" is a phrase linking the heavenly army to liturgical service. Formal register maintained throughout.*
